findings.description: Critical: packages/gen-eval/tests/test_integration_scenarios.py:45 and packages/gen-eval/tests/test_integration_orchestrator.py:34 still point package integration tests at the old repo-root evaluation/gen_eval/scenarios tree. I ran `cd packages/gen-eval && uv run pytest`; it collected 1059 tests and failed 7: `test_full_template_only_run` reported `report.total_scenarios == 0`, and every scenario-category integration test printed `Scenario directory not found: .../.git-worktrees/derive-descriptors-from-contracts/evaluation/gen_eval/scenarios/<category>`. The package Makefile's `test` target runs `uv run pytest -q -m "not slow"`, so it does not exclude these integration tests either. The CI unit command `uv run pytest -v -m "not e2e and not integration" --tb=short` passes, but the bare package test command requested for this review is not green.
findings.resolution: Either update the integration tests to point at the package-local scenarios that actually exist, restore/provide the repo-root scenario fixtures they expect, or change the package test target/default instructions to exclude integration tests consistently.

findings.description: Nit: openspec/changes/derive-descriptors-from-contracts/specs/gen-eval-framework/spec.md:215-227 still says descriptor reclamation `SHALL increment the descriptor contract version`, but I ran `cd packages/gen-eval && uv run python -c ...` and observed `CONTRACT_VERSION 2`, `VERSION_file 2`, and all three schemas, including `eval-report.schema.json`, carrying `x-gen-eval-contract-version 2`; `git diff -- packages/gen-eval/src/gen_eval/contracts/__init__.py ...` printed no diff versus the merge base. DOWNSTREAM.md:192-197 correctly says there is no second increment and that reclaiming a Python export is not a breaking JSON Schema change. The OpenSpec requirement is stale and contradicts the implemented state and the round-7 correction.
findings.resolution: Update the Descriptor Reclamation requirement/scenario to require a downstream notice and package-level export correction without requiring an additional JSON Schema contract-version bump.

findings.description: Archetype-aware descriptor loading is fixed. I ran `cd packages/gen-eval && uv run python -c ...` through `gen_eval.__main__.parse_args(['--descriptor','evaluation/descriptor.yaml'])` and `load_descriptor(args.descriptor)`; it printed `loaded_type ToolDescriptor`, `commands 1 interfaces 17 executable gen-eval`, and the resolved CLI contract path. The negative control `InterfaceDescriptor.from_yaml(args.descriptor)` printed `base_interfaces 0 base_has_commands False`, confirming the runtime path now preserves the derived fields that the base loader drops.

Operation-denominated `coverage_pct` is fixed. I constructed one `ServiceDescriptor` operation exposed on HTTP, MCP, and CLI, then built an orchestrator report with a single passing verdict for `GET /thing`; the command printed `all_interfaces ['GET /thing', 'mcp:get_thing', 'cli:thing get']`, `coverage_pct 100.0`, `unevaluated_operations []`, and `unevaluated_interfaces ['cli:thing get', 'mcp:get_thing']`. The headline number is now operation-denominated per D4 while still reporting unexercised sibling surfaces.

HTTP fan-in lookup is fixed. I constructed a `ServiceDescriptor` with operation `getThing` exposed as `GET /thing` and ran `operations_for_element`; the command printed `bare_http ['getThing']`, `prefixed_http ['getThing']`, and `mcp ['getThing']`. The public API no longer returns an empty list for HTTP elements.

OpenAPI `$ref` path items and path-level parameters are fixed. I generated a 3.1 document with `paths./items/{id}.$ref -> #/components/pathItems/ItemPath` and a path-level required `id` parameter, then ran `ServiceDescriptor.from_contract` and `verify_fastapi`; the command printed `operations [('getItem', [{'in': 'path', 'name': 'id', 'required': True, 'schema': {'type': 'string'}}])]`, `mcp_schema {'type': 'object', 'properties': {'id': {'type': 'string'}}, 'required': ['id']}`, `verify_extra []`, and the bad-reference control printed `bad_ref_error ValueError /bad: path item $ref '#/components/pathItems/Missing' resolves to nothing`. This is fail-closed and preserves path-item parameters in the derived input schema.

The argparse subset gate is no longer tautological. I temporarily inserted `--undeclared-review-probe` into the real `src/gen_eval/__main__.py` parser, then ran `cd packages/gen-eval && uv run pytest tests/test_subset_verifiers.py::TestAgainstGenEvalsOwnContract::test_the_real_parser_declares_nothing_the_contract_omits -q`; it failed with `gen-eval's argparse exposes flags its own CLI contract does not declare: ['cli:--undeclared-review-probe']`. I then restored `__main__.py`, cleared `src`/`tests` `__pycache__`, and `git status --short -- packages/gen-eval/src/gen_eval/__main__.py packages/gen-eval/tests` printed no changes.

The `--` option terminator is honored. I ran `_cli_identifiers` with `args=['--mode','template-only','--','--descriptor']` against gen-eval's declared surface; it printed `terminator ['cli:--mode']`. `cli:--descriptor` after the terminator was not credited.

Short-flag aliasing is fixed for descriptors that declare aliases. gen-eval's own contract printed `short_aliases {}` so `-v` correctly credits nothing there; with a probe `ToolDescriptor` declaring `FlagSpec(name='--verbose', short='-v')`, the command printed `declared {'cli:--verbose'}`, `aliases {'cli:-v': 'cli:--verbose'}`, and `short_v ['cli:--verbose']`.

`verify_argparse` now descends into subparsers. I built a real argparse parser with subcommand `run` and undocumented `--force`, plus a descriptor that only contracts the `run` command; `verify_argparse` printed `[('cli', 'cli:run --force')]`.

Dogfood threshold reachability is fixed. I ran `cd packages/gen-eval && make dogfood`; it exited 0 after `gen-eval: completed — 13/13 passed (100.0%)`, `gen-eval: PASS (pass rate 100.0% >= 100.0%; coverage 58.8% >= 1.0%)`, and `coverage complete: 10 of 17 units exercised (58.8%), 7 excluded with reasons`. The report probe printed `declared 17 coverage_pct 58.82352941176471` and the seven unevaluated units, matching the exclusions. The spec's 80% text is scoped to service dogfood, while tool dogfood is gated by completeness.

The runtime contract-version value itself is not bumped by this branch. I ran `cd packages/gen-eval && uv run python -c ...` and observed `CONTRACT_VERSION 2`, `VERSION_file 2`, and `eval-report.schema.json 2`, `interface-descriptor.schema.json 2`, `scenario.schema.json 2`; `git diff -- packages/gen-eval/src/gen_eval/contracts/__init__.py packages/gen-eval/src/gen_eval/contracts/eval-report.schema.json packages/gen-eval/README.md packages/gen-eval/evaluation/scenarios/contract-version.yaml openspec/changes/derive-descriptors-from-contracts/DOWNSTREAM.md` printed no diff versus the merge base for the runtime pins. This matches the round-7 rule that export-name reclamation is not a breaking schema change.
findings.resolution: No runtime change required; see finding 2 for stale spec text.

findings.description: `_merge_schemas` fails closed on incompatible shared-property schemas. I generated two OpenAPI operations bound to the same MCP element `shared`, both declaring query parameter `x` but with types `string` and `integer`; `ServiceDescriptor.from_contract(...).mcp_tools()` printed `schema_conflict ValueError mcp:shared: operations bound to this element declare incompatible schemas for 'x' — {'type': 'string'} vs {'type': 'integer'}`.

The `--min-coverage` unit ambiguity is fixed. I ran `cd packages/gen-eval && uv run gen-eval --descriptor evaluation/descriptor.yaml --output-dir evaluation/.reports/mincov-probe --fail-threshold 1.0 --min-coverage 0.8`; it exited 2 before evaluation and argparse printed `argument --min-coverage: 0.8 is a percent, so it means 0.8% ... If you meant 80%, pass 80`.

The new gates are empirically fail-capable. For the drift guard, I temporarily changed `evaluation/descriptor.yaml` from `project: gen-eval` to `project: gen-eval-review-drift` and ran `uv run python scripts/generate_tool_descriptor.py --check`; it exited 1 and printed `drift: .../evaluation/descriptor.yaml` plus a unified diff. For completeness, I fed temp reports/exclusions to `scripts/check_coverage_completeness.py`; it exited 1 for unexplained unevaluated units, blank reasons, stale exclusions, and zero declared surface, and exited 0 only for a matching non-blank exclusion. I restored the descriptor and `git status --short -- packages/gen-eval/evaluation/descriptor.yaml` printed no changes.

The deprecation-warning path is correctly scoped. I loaded a temp base descriptor with no `contract:` and a temp contract-backed tool descriptor through `load_descriptor`; the command printed `no_contract InterfaceDescriptor warnings [('DeprecationWarning', '<path> declares no `contract:`...')]` and `with_contract ToolDescriptor warnings []`.
